questions.text:
Write an essay on at least ONE visual or oral text that you have studied, in response to ONE of the statements below. Discuss the extent to which you agree with your chosen statement. Respond critically to the statement by making a close analysis of the text(s).

STATEMENTS (Choose ONE):
1. The most memorable texts use the interplay of image and sound to unsettle the audience.
2. A compelling antagonist forces the audience to question their own moral boundaries.
3. When a text disrupts the expected flow of time, it reveals deeper truths about human experience.
4. A bold director or creator uses discomfort as a tool to shift the audience's perspective.
5. The tension between characters is what gives a text its lasting power.
6. The details of a setting can carry as much meaning as the dialogue.
7. A single unexpected moment can redefine everything the audience thought they understood.
8. Characters who are shaped by their surroundings prompt us to reflect on our own circumstances.

You should aim to write a concise essay of no more than 5-6 pages in length. The quality of your writing is more important than the length of your essay.
questions.markingGuide:
ACHIEVED (3-4 marks): Present a structured response following essay conventions (some clumsiness in style or organisation is acceptable). Develop a relevant critical argument that provides an evaluative response to the chosen statement, showing engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate a range of relevant points showing understanding of the aspect(s) specified in the statement. Include specific and relevant details from the text(s) to support the argument. For visual or oral texts, reference specific techniques such as camera work, lighting, sound design, mise-en-scene, dialogue, or performance.

MERIT (5-6 marks): Present a structured response following essay conventions. Develop a convincing critical argument showing familiarity and engagement with the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing convincing understanding of the aspect(s) specified. Begin to weave specific details from the text(s) into the response to effectively support the argument. Potentially link the argument to matters beyond the text(s). Demonstrate understanding of how visual or oral techniques create meaning.

EXCELLENCE (7-8 marks): Present a cohesive and articulate response following essay conventions, showing some originality of expression. Develop a sophisticated and insightful or original critical argument showing familiarity with and appreciation of the text(s). Make and evaluate relevant points showing perceptive understanding of the aspect(s) specified. Weave specific and judiciously chosen relevant details from the text(s) into the response to effectively support and expand the argument. Link the argument to other aspects of the text or other contexts such as human experience, society, and the wider world.
